_doc: Prose for the drivetrain pages of the ACR Car Lab site (drivetrain_page.py). common.intro and common.rev_limit[source] (measured-past-curve when a measured limit is past the end of the torque curve) open every car's "How we worked it out"; cars[slug].workings follows. An item is a paragraph string; {"formula": [lines]}, a monospace formula block, where a line @paths, @final_drive or @primary is the car's computed formula lines (the same ones as the Final drive and Primary gear facts); {"list": [items]}, a numbered list; or "@name", which is common[name] (one item or a list of items). No number is typed here: {placeholders} are computed from calibration.json and the car's exported data. {factor} {fit_runs} {fit_car_count} {fit_cars} {rev_limit} {curve_end} (the last rpm of the torque curve) {adjustment} {fixed} {fixed_front} {fixed_rear} {fixed_apart}; {ratio:SPELLING}; {measured:RUN:GEAR} a measured km/h; {kmh:HYP:RUN:GEAR} the km/h a hypothesis predicts at the fitted factor; {apart:HYP1:HYP2:RUN} how far apart two hypotheses' total ratios are, in %; {off:HYP:RUN} the mean miss of a hypothesis over the run's fitted gears, in %; {speedratio:RUN1:RUN2} the mean ratio of two runs' measured speeds over the gears fitted in both. RUN is 1-based among the car's speed runs in calibration.json order. HYP is 'formula' (what the site uses) or a name in cars[slug].hypotheses: {path: average|front|rear, settings: {game name: spelling}, primary: spelling|times_set, rest: fixed_front|fixed_rear}. handling is an observation from test drives on 2026-09-13, shown word for word. User-visible text never names a person and never uses the word average: formulas are written out, with ÷ 2 (no-break spaces either side of the ÷, so it never starts a line).

intro: Every speed on these pages is worked out from engine revs and the gearing alone:

formula: speed (km/h) = rpm × tyre circumference (m) × 0.06 ÷ total ratio

intro: rpm × tyre circumference ÷ total ratio is metres per minute; × 0.06 (× 60 minutes per hour ÷ 1000 metres per kilometre) turns that into km/h.

formula: total ratio = primary × gear × final drive

intro: The free radius is the tyre radius stored in the game files. The rolling factor, {factor}, allows for a loaded tyre rolling on a slightly smaller radius; it was fitted to the top speeds measured in game on {fit_runs} runs across {fit_car_count} cars ({fit_cars}).

rev_limit.measured: The rev limit, {rev_limit} rpm, was measured in game with telemetry. The end of the torque curve in the game files is not the limiter: on most cars here the curve runs past it.
rev_limit.measured-past-curve: The rev limit, {rev_limit} rpm, was measured in game with telemetry. The torque curve in the game files ends at {curve_end} rpm, just short of the measured limit; on most other cars here it runs past the limit.
rev_limit.measured-stale: The rev limit, {rev_limit} rpm, was measured in game with telemetry on an earlier game version, and the car's engine data has changed since.
rev_limit.estimated: The rev limit, {rev_limit} rpm, is estimated from the shift-light rev stages in the game files. It has not been measured on this car.

common.centre_differential_why: With all four wheels turning at the same road speed, the centre differential's input turns at (front output speed + rear output speed) ÷ 2, so the equivalent final drive is:
single_ratio_untested: The final drive is {adjustment} alone, the one ratio below the gearbox in the game files:
The same rule fits the runs on the Stratos, the 037 and the GTA Junior (Differential Ratio Rear) and on the 306 Maxi (Differential Ratio Front). This car was not run.
common.set_primaries_per_set: Each gear set stores its own primary, and with no Primary Gear setting that primary is the one in force, as measured on the GTA Junior, whose gear sets all store 30//23. On this car the primary changes from one gear set to the next, and each set is taken to use its own in the same way; no car whose primary changes from set to set has been run.
fixed_awd_untested: Nothing below the gearbox is adjustable. The game files put a single fixed ratio, {fixed}, on the centre differential and 1 everywhere else, so the front and rear path ratios are both {fixed} and the final drive is that ratio:
The formula measured on the Delta Integrale, 206 WRC and Impreza gives the same number: ({fixed} + {fixed}) ÷ 2 = {fixed}. This car was not run.

workings: The final drive is Differential Ratio Rear alone, the one ratio below the gearbox in the game files:
The same rule fits the runs on the Stratos and the 037 (Differential Ratio Rear), on the 306 Maxi (Differential Ratio Front), and the run on this car below.
The GTA Junior has no Primary Gear setting, and every one of its gear sets stores a primary of 30//23 ({ratio:30//23}). The run was chosen to distinguish between two possibilities:

list: The gear set's stored primary applies: primary = 30//23.
The stored primary is ignored: primary = 1.

workings: It was run on gear set 1 with Differential Ratio Rear 43//9. The predictions for 3rd were about {kmh:formula:1:3} km/h under possibility 1 and {kmh:primary_ignored:1:3} km/h under possibility 2. The speedometer read {measured:1:3}, supporting possibility 1: primary = the gear set's own primary.
@single_ratio_untested

audi-quattro-gr4-1981.handling: No centre differential: different front and rear ratios make the axles fight and the car hard to control.
workings: The Quattro has no centre differential. Its front path has Differential Ratio Front and its rear path Differential Ratio Rear:
The final drive formula is taken from the Delta Integrale, 206 WRC and Impreza, where it was measured:

It cannot be tested here. A test needs different front and rear ratios, and with no centre differential they make the axles fight and the car hard to control. With both set the same, as the car ships, the final drive is simply that ratio.

On the Xsara, Center Differential Ratio is the only ratio setup offers, and it is applied before the centre differential. The front and rear differentials are fixed in the game files, {fixed_front} at the front and {fixed_rear} at the rear:
@centre_differential_why
The one run could not distinguish between three possibilities:

list: Final drive = front path ratio alone.
Final drive = rear path ratio alone.
Final drive = (front path ratio + rear path ratio) ÷ 2.

workings: It was run on gear set 1 with Center Differential Ratio 39//24. The two fixed differentials are only {fixed_apart}% apart, so all three put 6th at about {kmh:formula:1:6} km/h, too close to distinguish with the in-game speedometer. The speedometer read {measured:1:6}. It fits final drive = (front path ratio + rear path ratio) ÷ 2, the formula measured on the Delta Integrale, 206 WRC and Impreza.
@single_ratio_untested
@set_primaries_per_set
@single_ratio_untested
@set_primaries_per_set
@fixed_awd_untested
The final drive is Differential Ratio Rear alone, the one ratio below the gearbox in the game files:

A run on gear set 2 with Differential Ratio Rear 46//9 fits that formula: the speedometer read {measured:1:5} km/h in 5th, where it puts 5th at {kmh:formula:1:5}. That run is also one of those the rolling factor was fitted on.

On the Delta the game files put Center Differential Ratio before the centre differential. The front drivetrain path has no additional selectable reduction; the rear path adds Center Ratio to Rear and Differential Ratio Rear:
@centre_differential_why
The first run could not distinguish between two possibilities:

list: The selected Center Ratio to Rear and Differential Ratio Rear are ignored and their stock values stay in effect: final drive = Center Differential Ratio × 13//34 × 30//12.
Final drive = (front path ratio + rear path ratio) ÷ 2, with the selected rear ratios.

workings: It was run on Center Differential Ratio 55//12 with the rear ratios close to stock: Center Ratio to Rear 13//34 and Differential Ratio Rear 34//14. With those settings the two possibilities put 6th at about {kmh:rear_ignored:1:6} and {kmh:formula:1:6} km/h, only about {apart:rear_ignored:formula:1}% apart, too little to distinguish reliably with the in-game speedometer. The speedometer read {measured:1:6}.

For the second run Center Differential Ratio stayed on 55//12 and the rear ratios were deliberately moved far from stock: Center Ratio to Rear 17//38 and Differential Ratio Rear 34//13. This produced clearly different predictions for 6th: about {kmh:rear_ignored:2:6} km/h under possibility 1, or {kmh:formula:2:6} km/h under possibility 2. The measured speed was {measured:2:6} km/h, supporting final drive = (front path ratio + rear path ratio) ÷ 2.
@single_ratio_untested
@set_primaries_per_set
The Stratos has a Primary Gear setting, and its gear sets also store a primary of their own, 33//31*31//30 ({ratio:33//31*31//30}). The runs distinguish between:

list: The Primary Gear you pick replaces the gear set's primary: primary = Primary Gear.
The Primary Gear you pick multiplies it: primary = Primary Gear × 33//31*31//30.

workings: All three gear sets were run on Primary Gear 35//30*33//28 with Differential Ratio Rear 65//17. On gear set 3 the predictions for 5th were about {kmh:formula:3:5} km/h if it replaces and {kmh:times_set:3:5} km/h if it multiplies. The speedometer read {measured:3:5}, and gear sets 1 and 2 agreed, supporting primary = Primary Gear.
The primary is the Primary Gear you pick. The final drive is Differential Ratio Rear alone, the one ratio below the gearbox in the game files:
@single_ratio_untested
@set_primaries_per_set

peugeot-206-wrc-1999.handling: Setting the front and rear ratios far apart can make the car handle oddly.
workings: On the 206, Center Differential Ratio is applied before the centre differential. The front path adds Differential Ratio Front and the rear path Differential Ratio Rear:
@centre_differential_why
Its gear sets store a primary of 20//25, which is not one of the three Primary Gear steps. The first two runs distinguish between:

list: The Primary Gear you pick replaces the stored primary: primary = Primary Gear.
The stored primary still applies: primary = 20//25.

workings: Gear set 1 was run on Primary Gear 21//24 and gear set 3 on 22//24. On gear set 1 the predictions for 3rd were about {kmh:formula:1:3} km/h with primary = Primary Gear and {kmh:set_primary:1:3} km/h with primary = 20//25. The speedometer read {measured:1:3}. Across the gears, 20//25 would have put the speeds about {off:set_primary:1}% too high on gear set 1 and {off:set_primary:2}% too high on gear set 3, supporting primary = Primary Gear.
The third run was chosen to distinguish between:

list: Center Differential Ratio multiplies the whole final drive.
Center Differential Ratio does not change the gearing.

workings: It repeated the second run with Center Differential Ratio on 31//21 ({ratio:31//21}) instead of 24//24 (a ratio of 1). The predictions for 5th were about {kmh:formula:3:5} km/h if it multiplies and {kmh:cdr_ignored:3:5} km/h if it changes nothing. The speedometer read {measured:3:5}, and across the gears the speeds dropped by a factor of about {speedratio:2:3} from the second run, supporting possibility 1: Center Differential Ratio multiplies the whole final drive.
The last run was chosen to distinguish between:

list: Final drive = front path ratio alone.
Final drive = rear path ratio alone.
Final drive = (front path ratio + rear path ratio) ÷ 2.

workings: It was run on gear set 3 with Primary Gear 22//24, Center Differential Ratio 24//24, Differential Ratio Front 43//13*21//13 and Differential Ratio Rear 40//18*26//16. The three possibilities put 4th at about {kmh:front:4:4}, {kmh:rear:4:4} and {kmh:formula:4:4} km/h. The speedometer read {measured:4:4}, supporting final drive = (front path ratio + rear path ratio) ÷ 2.
Nothing below the gearbox is adjustable. The game files put a single fixed ratio, {fixed}, on the front differential, and the final drive is that ratio:
This car was not run.
The final drive is Differential Ratio Front alone, the one ratio below the gearbox in the game files:

A run on gear set 4 with Differential Ratio Front 68//12 fits that formula: the speedometer read {measured:1:6} km/h in 6th, where it puts 6th at {kmh:formula:1:6}. That run is also one of those the rolling factor was fitted on.
@fixed_awd_untested

subaru-impreza-555-s3-1993.handling: Setting the front and rear ratios far apart can make the car handle oddly.
workings: On the Impreza no ratio is applied before the centre differential. The front path has Differential Ratio Front; the rear path has Center Ratio to Rear and Differential Ratio Rear:
@centre_differential_why
The first run was chosen to distinguish between:

list: Final drive = front path ratio alone.
Final drive = rear path ratio alone.
Final drive = (front path ratio + rear path ratio) ÷ 2.

workings: It was run on Differential Ratio Front 36//7 and Differential Ratio Rear 31//9, with Center Ratio to Rear on 31//31, a ratio of 1. The three possibilities put 5th at about {kmh:front:1:5}, {kmh:rear:1:5} and {kmh:formula:1:5} km/h. The speedometer read {measured:1:5}, supporting final drive = (front path ratio + rear path ratio) ÷ 2.
The second run was chosen to distinguish between:

list: Center Ratio to Rear multiplies: rear path ratio = Center Ratio to Rear × Differential Ratio Rear.
Center Ratio to Rear is ignored: rear path ratio = Differential Ratio Rear.
Center Ratio to Rear divides: rear path ratio = Differential Ratio Rear ÷ Center Ratio to Rear.

workings: It was run on Differential Ratio Front 31//9, Center Ratio to Rear 22//28 and Differential Ratio Rear 48//11. If Center Ratio to Rear multiplies, these keep the two path ratios nearly equal. The three possibilities put 4th at about {kmh:formula:2:4}, {kmh:ctr_ignored:2:4} and {kmh:ctr_divides:2:4} km/h. The speedometer read {measured:2:4}, supporting rear path ratio = Center Ratio to Rear × Differential Ratio Rear. With the path ratios nearly equal the car drove normally, as expected.
@fixed_awd_untested
